findings.detail: The reason for option D says the guide recommends tables for 'financial and numeric data'. The guide (5.6-S5) only says financial data should be rendered as tables. It does not mention numeric data in general, so the reason misstates the guide.

This question has the same problem as the earlier question M3-S46-T1, also in scenario 2 with Claude Code. Claude Code reads old design documents and other mixed-age sources and misreads a temporal difference: as a contradiction there, as a false decline here. Both are fixed by adding source dates to each structured finding. The same reasoning leads to the same correct action, so this is not a different problem such as the cause against the fix or a choice between rules.

blind_answer.reason: The trend was reported backwards because the extracted entries had no dates, so Claude Code could not tell which figure came first. Requiring a publication or collection date on each entry fixes this (5.6-K4/S4). Averaging the figures hides the trend, confidence scores don't establish order, and a table changes presentation without fixing the time ordering.
